**From left to right**, the **exact values** of the $x$-intercepts of the parabola shown above are{{field-1}}
and 
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(1,2)$ and passes through the point $(3,-2).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(1,2)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4p(y-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(3,-2),$ we substitute $x=3$ and $y=-2$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-1)^{2} & =4p(-2-2) \\ 4 & =4p(-4) \\ p & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =-(y-2).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =-(0-2) \\ (x-1)^{2} & =2 \\ x-1 & =\pm \sqrt{2} \\ x & =1\pm \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $1-\sqrt{2}$  and $1+\sqrt{2}.$
